symptom: ako/mxcli#1868 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1710, 11.12.4): `declare $L String = 'x' + if $c then 'a' else 'b';` passed check ("Syntax OK", "Check passed!") and exec, and mx check failed CE0117
cause: MDL's expression grammar admits an if-expression at any primary position, Mendix's only where a whole expression goes; the writer stores the source as written, so the unparenthesised operand reached the model. No rule compared the two grammars
file: mdl/executor/validate_if_operand.go (ifOperands, checkIfOperand, called from checkExprFunctions so microflows and nanoflows share it), mdl/executor/validate.go (execEnforcedMicroflowRules)
fix: MDL-IFOPERAND01 error, exec-enforced: an IfThenElseExpr as a direct operand of a binary operator or a unary minus, with the parenthesised form as the fix
test: mdl/executor/if_operand_test.go — +, and, =, unary minus, return, nanoflow, check/exec agreement; controls parenthesised, else-branch absorbing the +, function argument, not() argument, if as else branch. Revert (hook call commented out): the five bad shapes and the nanoflow and agreement tests failed. Measured on mxbuild 11.12.2, one microflow per shape and mx check -j to attribute each error: every bad shape CE0117, every control clean
insight: mx check prints the element ("Create variable activity 'Create Boolean variable'"), not the microflow, so a one-microflow-per-shape matrix is unattributable from the console; `mx check -j out.json` carries document-name per error. The boundary was not the operator but the position: `if … else 'b' + 'x'` builds because the else branch takes the `+`, so a rule on `+ if` in the source text would have been right by accident and wrong for `-if`
